learn.title: Arrays that grow
learn.body: A normal array has a fixed size. With the heap you can start small and grow when you run out. `realloc(ptr, newSize)` changes the size of a heap block and keeps the old contents. It may move the block, so always use the pointer it returns.

learn.title: Doubling when full
learn.body: Start with room for 2 ints and add 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Each time `n == cap`, double the capacity. The program prints `5 8 50`: five items, capacity 8, last value 50. The loop is not shown here.

learn.title: Why the extra variable
learn.body: If `realloc` fails it returns `NULL` but leaves the old block untouched. Writing `a = realloc(a, ...)` would overwrite your only pointer to that block and leak it. Store the result in `t`, check it, then copy it into `a`.

learn.title: Following the capacity
learn.body: Trace the capacity as items 1 to 5 are added, starting at 2.
Doubling means fewer calls and fewer copies than growing by one each time. Free the final block once, at the end.

choices: Resizes a heap block and keeps its contents
questions.explanation: It grows or shrinks a block, copying the old data if it must move.
With `a = realloc(a, ...)` a failure would lose the old pointer.

questions.prompt: Start with capacity 2 and double it twice. What is the capacity?
What does the example print as the last value?
After a successful `realloc`, use the \_\_ pointer.
questions.explanation: The block may have moved, so the old pointer can no longer be trusted.

questions.prompt: How many times should the final block be freed?
questions.explanation: `realloc` already released the old blocks. Free the final one once.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of adding to a full array in order.
steps: Check it is not `NULL`, then store it in `a`
questions.explanation: Check before you replace your only pointer.
